kaps_punt: Kenmerke van die Aarde: die aarde is rond soos 'n bal (sfeer) en is gemaak van rots; die belangrikste oppervlaktes van die Aarde is land (rotse en grond), water en lug; die meeste van die oppervlak van die Aarde is bedek met water (oseane en seë); die land wat ons kan sien, is gemaak van kontinente en eilande; daar is 'n dun laag van lug rondom die Aarde; die Aarde het baie verskillende habitatte vir lewende dinge

items.bewering: Die grond onder jou voete lyk plat tot by die verste bome.
items.blok: Die Aarde is 'n bal met rots aan die buitekant
items.bron: This is a statement about how things look, not a measurement. 'verste' is ordinary description and makes no ranking claim. It is consistent with Earth's curvature being too gentle to see over short distances (the Earth is a near-sphere with a radius of about 6 371 km; earthhow.com/shape-of-the-earth, home.csulb.edu/~rodrigue/geog140/lectures/earthinspace.html).

items.bewering: Tog is die hele Aarde rond soos 'n groot bal.
items.blok: Die Aarde is 'n bal met rots aan die buitekant
items.bron: The Earth is an oblate spheroid flattened by about 1 part in 298, so it is very nearly a sphere and looks round from space (home.csulb.edu/~rodrigue/geog140/lectures/earthinspace.html; earthhow.com/shape-of-the-earth). Mapping checked: 'round like a ball' carries only shape, and the block itself immediately cuts off the one place a learner could go wrong (the Earth is 'not hollow like a soccer ball'). The mapping holds.

items.bewering: Mense in ruimtetuie het dit self gesien.
items.blok: Die Aarde is 'n bal met rots aan die buitekant
items.bron: Apollo 8 (Borman, Lovell, Anders, December 1968) were the first humans to see the Earth as a whole planet. Apollo 17 photographed the whole sunlit disc in 1972 (the Blue Marble). Sources: NASA 'Apollo 8: Earthrise' (nasa.gov/image-article/apollo-8-earthrise/), NASA 'Earth Viewed by Apollo 8' (science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/earth-viewed-by-apollo-8-36019/), NASA 'Blue Marble - Image of the Earth from Apollo 17' (nasa.gov/image-article/blue-marble-image-of-earth-from-apollo-17/).

items.bewering: 'n Vorm wat rond soos 'n bal is, noem ons 'n sfeer.
items.blok: Die Aarde is 'n bal met rots aan die buitekant
items.bron: This is the standard meaning of sphere/sfeer (a perfectly round solid, the shape of a ball). It is consistent with the descriptions of Earth as 'nearly spherical' in the shape sources above (home.csulb.edu geog140; earthhow.com).

items.bewering: Die buitenste deel van hierdie groot bal is van rots gemaak.
items.blok: Die Aarde is 'n bal met rots aan die buitekant
items.bron: The crust is Earth's thin, solid outermost layer. It is made of rock under both the oceans (mostly basalt) and the continents (mostly granitic rock): National Geographic Education 'crust' (media.nationalgeographic.org/assets/reference/assets/crust-3.pdf); JoVE 'Earth's crust'. Read against the rest of the lesson: the heading says 'rots aan die buitekant', and the next blocks say the surface is the 'buitekant' and is mostly covered by water. The lesson places water and air 'op en om hierdie bal' and says water 'bedek' the surface, so the picture is a rock ball with water lying on it. That is correct, because the crust under the oceans is rock too. No contradiction.

items.bewering: Breek 'n stuk van 'n berg af en jy hou harde rots vas.
items.blok: Die Aarde is 'n bal met rots aan die buitekant
items.bron: Mountains are landforms of the crust, which is made of rock: continental crust is mostly granitic rock and is thickest, up to about 70 km, under mountain ranges (National Geographic 'crust' PDF; JoVE 'Earth's crust'). Some mountains are partly loose material or ice, but this sentence is an example of the rock crust, not a rule about every mountain.

items.bewering: Maar die Aarde is nie hol soos 'n sokkerbal nie.
items.blok: Die Aarde is 'n bal met rots aan die buitekant
items.bron: The interior is solid and liquid all the way through: a rock mantle making up about 84% of Earth's volume, a liquid outer core and a solid inner core. Sources: USGS 'The Interior of the Earth' (pubs.usgs.gov/gip/interior/); National Geographic Education 'Mantle' and 'Core'. Mapping checked: the comparison is used to deny hollowness, which is exactly where 'like a ball' could mislead. The lesson does not say what the inside is made of, so it makes no false claim about the core.

items.bewering: Die Aarde se oppervlak is die hele buitekant van die groot bal.
items.bron: This is the ordinary meaning of a surface (the outside of a thing). It is consistent with NOAA and USGS, who speak of the surface as the area that water and land cover (globalocean.noaa.gov/the-ocean/; usgs.gov/media/images/distribution-water-and-above-earth).

items.bewering: Die drie belangrikste dinge op en om hierdie bal is land, water en lug.
items.bron: 'belangrikste' is a framing, not a ranking that can be measured. It matches the standard Earth-system description. NASA describes the geosphere (rocks, sediments, soils), hydrosphere and atmosphere, with the biosphere as a fourth sphere. A NOAA teacher guide puts it as 'land, water, living things, or air' (mynasadata.larc.nasa.gov 'Spheres of Earth'; gml.noaa.gov/infodata/info_activities/pdfs/TBI_earth_spheres.pdf). The lesson lists living things separately in its last block, so the set of three does not exclude anything falsely.

items.bewering: Die land is die rotse en die grond waarop jy elke dag loop.
items.bron: NASA's geosphere/lithosphere is the solid part of Earth: rocks, sediments and soils, and surface landforms (mynasadata.larc.nasa.gov 'Spheres of Earth' lesson plan).

items.bewering: Die water lê in die see en ook in riviere en mere.
items.bron: NOAA: about 97% of Earth's water is in the ocean, and the rest is in glaciers and ice, below ground, and in rivers and lakes (oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/wherewater.html). The sentence does not claim to be a complete list, so leaving out ice and groundwater is not false.

items.bewering: Die lug is oral bo die land en bo die water.
items.bron: The atmosphere surrounds the whole planet, over land and sea alike (NASA 'Earth's Atmosphere: A Multi-layered Cake', science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-atmosphere/earths-atmosphere-a-multi-layered-cake/; NASA FETTSS 'Earth Atmosphere').

items.bewering: Elke foto wys net een kant van die groot bal.
items.bron: A single view from space shows at most one hemisphere, and only its sunlit part can be seen. Even DSCOVR/EPIC, sitting a million miles away on the Sun-Earth line, captures 'the entire sunlit face', not the whole globe (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11924; planetary.org/articles/07201148-dscovr-epic-globe-earth).

items.bewering: Al die kante saam wys baie meer blou as bruin en groen.
items.bron: Water covers about 71% of the surface and land about 29%, a ratio of roughly 2.4 to 1 (USGS, usgs.gov/media/images/distribution-water-and-above-earth; NOAA, globalocean.noaa.gov/the-ocean/). Tested with the colour statements in the next block as a set: some land shows white rather than brown or green (Antarctica under its ice). That only makes 'more blue than brown and green' more true, not less.

items.bewering: Die blou is water, en dit bedek die grootste deel van die Aarde se oppervlak.
items.bron: About 71% of Earth's surface is covered by water (USGS, usgs.gov/media/images/distribution-water-and-above-earth; NOAA Global Ocean Monitoring, globalocean.noaa.gov/the-ocean/; NPS trivia card, nps.gov/cham/learn/kidsyouth/trivia17.htm). The oceans appear blue in photographs from space: NASA's Blue Marble caption (nasa.gov/image-article/blue-marble-image-of-earth-from-apollo-17/).

items.bewering: Die meeste van hierdie water lê in die oseane en die seë.
items.bron: The oceans hold about 96.5% of all Earth's water (USGS) or about 97% (NOAA, oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/wherewater.html). Seas are marginal parts of the ocean (NOAA, oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/oceanorsea.html).

items.bewering: 'n Oseaan is 'n baie groot see wat ver oor die Aarde strek.
items.bron: Oxford's first sense is 'a large expanse of sea, esp. each of the main areas called the Atlantic, Pacific, Indian, Arctic, and Antarctic Oceans' (Oxford entry as reproduced at bible.sabda.org/lexicon.php?word=ocean; oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/ocean). NOAA: seas are smaller than oceans and are usually partly enclosed by land (oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/oceanorsea.html). So an ocean being bigger than a sea, and spread over a wide area, is correct.

items.bewering: Die water in oseane en seë is sout, en jy kan dit nie drink nie.
items.bron: Seawater averages about 35 parts per thousand of salt. Humans cannot safely drink it, because the kidneys must pass more water than was drunk to get rid of the salt, which leads to dehydration (NOAA, oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/drinksw.html; USGS, water.usgs.gov/edu/saline.html). Some lakes are named 'seas', but this does not affect the statement, because the lesson defines seas as part of the ocean.

items.bewering: Die bruin en die groen dele op daardie foto's is die land.
items.bron: In whole-Earth photographs, land shows as brown (deserts) and green (vegetation). NASA's caption for the Apollo 17 Blue Marble identifies Africa, the Arabian Peninsula and Madagascar as the land in the frame (nasa.gov/image-article/blue-marble-image-of-earth-from-apollo-17/). The sentence does not say that all land is brown or green. Ice-covered land shows white, and the lesson deals with that separately under 'poolkappe'.

items.bewering: Die land wat jy kan sien, bestaan uit kontinente en eilande.
items.bron: Land above sea level is divided into continents and islands, and nearby islands are usually counted with a continent (National Geographic encyclopedic entry 'continent', media.nationalgeographic.org/assets/reference/assets/continent-3.pdf; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continent).

items.bewering: 'n Kontinent is een van die groter stukke land op die Aarde se oppervlak.
items.bron: National Geographic Education: a continent is 'one of Earth's seven main divisions of land' (media.nationalgeographic.org/assets/reference/assets/continent-3.pdf). Wikipedia: continents are identified by convention rather than by strict criteria (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continent). 'stuk' read as a portion of land, rather than a separate piece, also covers Europe and Asia, which are one landmass. A Grade 4 learner is unlikely to reason there, and the wording does not say the pieces must be separate.

items.bewering: 'n Ander woord vir 'n kontinent is 'n vasteland.
items.bron: Afrikaans Wikipedia opens 'Kontinent' with "'n Kontinent of vasteland is enige van 'n aantal groot geografiese streke op land", and uses 'die vasteland van Europa' and 'die vasteland van Australië' (af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kontinent). Afrikaans Wiktionary defines vasteland as "'n groot aaneenlopende landmassa" with the synonym 'kontinent' (af.wiktionary.org/wiki/vasteland). Note for the writer, not a fault: vasteland also means 'mainland', that is land as opposed to an island (vocabulary.com/dictionary/nl/vasteland, Dutch). The synonym claim is still true. I did not reach the WAT or the HAT entry itself.

items.bewering: Afrika is 'n kontinent, en Suid-Afrika lê aan sy suidpunt.
items.bron: SANParks: Agulhas National Park lies at Cape Agulhas and covers 'the southernmost tip of the African continent' (sanparks.org/parks/agulhas). Cape Agulhas is in South Africa's Western Cape (gov.za media statement on the Map of Africa monument at Agulhas, gov.za/news/media-statements/minister-derek-hanekom-launches-iconic-map-africa-monument-agulhas-national).

items.bewering: 'n Eiland is 'n stuk land met water reg rondom.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'List of islands by area', and Britannica's definition as quoted by a secondary source (todayifoundout.com, 'Why Greenland is an Island and Australia is a Continent'): an island is land completely surrounded by water and smaller than a continent. Tested together with the next sentence as a pair: 'water all round' on its own would make Australia an island. The next sentence ('selfs 'n groot eiland is kleiner as 'n kontinent') and the begrip entry ('kleiner as 'n kontinent') add the size condition, which is the conventional way to settle it. Together they are consistent.

items.bewering: Selfs 'n groot eiland is kleiner as 'n kontinent.
items.bron: Greenland, the largest island, is about 2.11 million km². Australia, the smallest continent, is about 7.59 million km², more than three times as large (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_islands_by_area). By convention, continental landmasses are not classed as islands, and Britannica's definition (quoted at todayifoundout.com) has islands 'smaller than a continent'. True as the convention.

items.bewering: 'n Boot kan heeltemal om Robbeneiland naby Kaapstad vaar.
items.bron: Robben Island lies in Table Bay, about 11 km offshore according to the Department of Arts and Culture and UNESCO (dac.gov.za/content/robben-island; whc.unesco.org/document/139687), or about 6.9 km west of Bloubergstrand. It is about 3.3 km by 1.9 km and surrounded by open water (sahistory.org.za/article/robben-island; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robben_Island). 'naby Kaapstad' is correct. That a boat can go right round it follows from it being an island in open, navigable Table Bay, and boat cruises sail past it regularly (sa-venues.com Robben Island cruise). I found no source that describes a full circuit as a route, but the claim is about what is possible, not about a tour.

items.bewering: 'n Meer is 'n stuk water met land reg rondom.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's: 'a large area of water that is surrounded by land' (oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/lake). Wikipedia: lakes lie in a basin surrounded by land and are separate from the ocean (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake).

items.bewering: 'n Eiland is land in die water, en 'n meer is water in die land.
items.bron: This is a mirror contrast built from the two definitions above (island: land surrounded by water; lake: water surrounded by land; sources as above). Mapping checked as a pair: the reversal is exact, and pushing it further does not mislead. An island can lie in a lake or a river as well as the sea, which is still 'land in die water'. The contrast holds.

items.bewering: 'n Poolkap is 'n groot wit laag ys heel in die noorde of heel in die suide van die Aarde.
items.bron: A polar ice cap is a high-latitude region covered in ice (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_ice_cap). The Antarctic ice cap is visible as white in the Apollo 17 Blue Marble (NASA, nasa.gov/image-article/blue-marble-image-of-earth-from-apollo-17/, which calls it 'the Antarctic south polar ice cap'). Note, not a fault: geologists use 'ice cap' strictly for smaller land ice and call Antarctica an 'ice sheet'. The northern cap is floating sea ice on the Arctic Ocean. The lesson says 'laag ys' and does not say whether it lies on land or water, so neither point makes it false.

items.bewering: Poolkappe lê by die Noordpool en by die Suidpool.
items.bron: The North Pole is covered by floating pack ice over the Arctic Ocean. The South Pole is on Antarctica, under the Antarctic ice sheet of almost 14 million km² (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_ice_cap). Arctic sea ice is shrinking but still covers the pole (NSIDC/NASA on the 2026 Arctic maximum, science.nasa.gov/earth/arctic-winter-sea-ice-2026/).

items.bewering: Dit is van die koudste plekke op die hele Aarde.
items.bron: NASA's 'Which Pole Is Colder?' gives winter averages of about −40 °C at the North Pole and about −60 °C at the South Pole (science.nasa.gov/kids/earth/which-pole-is-colder/). The world's lowest recorded temperature, −89.2 °C, was at Vostok Station in Antarctica (Guinness World Records; Scientific American). The softened form 'van die koudste' is right: the South Pole region is the coldest, but the North Pole is not the coldest place in the Northern Hemisphere (Siberia and the Greenland ice cap are colder; earthsky.org). It is still among the coldest places, which is all the sentence claims.

items.bewering: Jy kan mere en poolkappe op 'n foto van die Aarde uitwys.
items.bron: The Antarctic polar ice cap is visible in the Apollo 17 whole-Earth photograph (nasa.gov/image-article/blue-marble-image-of-earth-from-apollo-17/). Large lakes are clearly visible in astronaut photographs from the ISS, for example the Great Lakes (earthobservatory.nasa.gov/images/146632/great-lakes-without-winter-ice), and in satellite images of Lake Victoria (visibleearth.nasa.gov/images/54749/lake-victoria). Only large lakes show up, and the sentence does not claim more.

items.bewering: Jy kan nie lug sien nie, maar jy voel dit as die wind waai.
items.bron: Wind is 'air in motion relative to the surface of the earth' (American Meteorological Society Glossary of Meteorology, glossary.ametsoc.org/wiki/wind/). Merriam-Webster describes air as a mixture of 'invisible odorless tasteless gases' (quoted in the KIT materials vocabulary entry 'Air', matwerk.datamanager.kit.edu). The blue of the sky comes from scattered sunlight and is not air being seen, so the statement stands at this level.

items.bewering: 'n Dun laag lug lê om die hele Aarde.
items.bron: NASA: 99.99997% of the atmosphere lies below the Kármán line at 100 km (science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-atmosphere/earths-atmosphere-a-multi-layered-cake/), against an Earth radius of about 6 371 km. NOAA JetStream: half of the air molecules lie within the first 5.6 km (noaa.gov/jetstream/atmosphere/air-pressure). It is thin relative to the planet.

items.bewering: Dit lê oor die land, die see en die poolkappe.
items.bron: The atmosphere envelops the whole planet (NASA 'Earth's Atmosphere: A Multi-layered Cake'; NASA FETTSS 'Earth Atmosphere', fettss.arc.nasa.gov/collection/details/earth-atmosphere/).

items.bewering: As jy opkyk, lyk die lug eindeloos. Maar van die ruimte af lyk dit soos 'n baie dun lagie om die groot bal.
items.bron: ISS limb photographs show the atmosphere as a 'thin blue' band at Earth's edge (NASA 'Thin Blue Line', nasa.gov/image-article/thin-blue-line/; images.nasa.gov iss059e027932; eol.jsc.nasa.gov ISS023-E-57948 caption: 'gradually fades into the blackness of outer space'). Mapping checked: 'lagie' could suggest a layer with a clean top edge, but the same block says straight away that there is no top edge and that the air thins gradually. That is exactly the correction the comparison needs.

items.bewering: Hoe hoër jy gaan, hoe minder lug is daar.
items.bron: NOAA JetStream: air becomes less dense as elevation increases (noaa.gov/jetstream/atmosphere/air-pressure; noaa.gov/jetstream/radar-beams).

items.bewering: Nêrens hou dit skielik op nie, en daar is geen boonste rand nie.
items.bron: NASA SVS: 'no hard and fast line divides Earth's upper atmosphere from outer space' (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/12823). NASA APOD: there is no sharp physical boundary (science.nasa.gov/image-article/apod-2021-july-24-the-edge-of-space/). UCAR: no clear-cut upper boundary where the exosphere fades into space (scied.ucar.edu/learning-zone/atmosphere/exosphere). The Kármán line is a convention, not a physical edge.

items.bewering: Mense en baie diere asem die lug van hierdie dun laag in.
items.bron: Air-breathing animals take their oxygen from the atmosphere, and the atmosphere is about 21% oxygen (composition quoted from Britannica via the KIT vocabulary entry; NASA 'The Atmosphere: Earth's Security Blanket', science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-atmosphere/the-atmosphere-earths-security-blanket/). 'baie diere' rightly leaves out animals such as fish, which take oxygen from water.

items.bewering: Die land, die water en die lug vorm saam baie soorte plekke.
items.bron: NASA describes the biosphere as life on land, in the oceans and rivers, and so on, across the geosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere (mynasadata.larc.nasa.gov 'Spheres of Earth'; education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/earths-systems/).

items.bewering: 'n Habitat is die plek waar 'n plant of 'n dier lewe.
items.bron: National Geographic Education: 'A habitat is a place where an organism makes its home' (education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/habitat/). Vocabulary.com: 'the native habitat or home of an animal or plant'. Restricting it to plants and animals is a Grade 4 simplification and not false.

items.bewering: Die see is die habitat van baie visse en ook van robbe.
items.bron: Cape fur seals are primarily marine and spend much of their time at sea feeding. They also haul out on rocky shores, beaches and offshore islands to rest, breed and moult (summary of Cape fur seal at-sea habitat studies, Inter-Research MEPS v649 p201-218; Deakin University study of female Cape fur seal at-sea habitat use). Tested as a set against the springbok sentence: sea animals against land animals is a true contrast. The sentence says the sea is a habitat of seals, not their only one, so it is incomplete but not false. Fish obviously live in the sea.

items.bewering: 'n Grasveld op die land is die habitat van 'n springbok.
items.bron: SANBI Red List of South African Species: springbok 'key habitats are thus open grasslands (particularly the short grass fringes of pans), arid shrubveld (Karoo)...'. The species formerly occurred in huge numbers in the dry grasslands and shrublands of southern Africa (speciesstatus.sanbi.org/assessment/last-assessment/1940/). Britannica: open, treeless plains (britannica.com/animal/springbok-mammal). Grassland is one of the springbok's habitats, which is all the sentence claims.

items.bewering: Die Aarde het baie verskillende habitatte, en daarom is daar baie soorte lewende dinge.
items.bron: Stein, Gerstner and Kreft (2014, Ecology Letters), a meta-analysis of 192 studies: environmental and habitat heterogeneity has a significant positive effect on species richness, which they describe as a universal driver across taxa and biomes (publications.goettingen-research-online.de/ID-5795). The mechanism is more niches and refuges. Habitat diversity is not the only cause of biodiversity, but 'daarom' as a Grade 4 causal link is supported.

items.bewering: Begrip 'sfeer': Die naam vir 'n vorm wat rond soos 'n bal is.
items.bron: Same meaning as in the study text, checked above (Earth as a near-sphere: home.csulb.edu geog140; earthhow.com).

items.bewering: Begrip 'oppervlak': Die hele buitekant van 'n ding.
items.bron: This is the ordinary meaning of surface. It matches the study block 'Land, water en lug', checked above.

items.bewering: Begrip 'oseaan': 'n Baie groot see wat ver oor die Aarde strek.
items.bron: Oxford: 'a large expanse of sea'. NOAA: seas are smaller than oceans (oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/oceanorsea.html). The entry reads correctly on its own.

items.bewering: Begrip 'kontinent': Een van die groter stukke land op die Aarde se oppervlak. Dit word ook 'n vasteland genoem.
items.bron: National Geographic: 'one of Earth's seven main divisions of land'. Afrikaans Wikipedia: "'n Kontinent of vasteland..." (af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kontinent). Read on its own, 'een van die groter stukke' could let a learner count a big island. The eiland entry ('kleiner as 'n kontinent') closes that, so the pair is consistent.

items.bewering: Begrip 'eiland': 'n Stuk land met water rondom, kleiner as 'n kontinent.
items.bron: Britannica as quoted at todayifoundout.com: islands are 'smaller than a continent'. Greenland (about 2.11 million km²) is smaller than Australia (about 7.59 million km²) (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_islands_by_area). It reads correctly on its own.

items.bewering: Begrip 'poolkap': 'n Groot laag ys by die Noordpool of by die Suidpool van die Aarde.
items.bron: Polar ice cap: a high-latitude region covered in ice. Floating pack ice in the north and the Antarctic ice sheet in the south (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_ice_cap; NASA Blue Marble caption 'Antarctic south polar ice cap'). It reads correctly on its own.

items.bewering: Begrip 'habitat': Die plek waar 'n plant of 'n dier lewe.
items.bron: National Geographic Education: 'A habitat is a place where an organism makes its home' (education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/habitat/). It reads correctly on its own.

opsomming: Every one of the 51 claims checked out against sources, including all superlatives and comparisons and the paired contrasts (island and lake, island and continent, sea animals and land animals, blue and brown or green). Nothing has to change. A person may want to know three things: 'vasteland' also means 'mainland'; seals use the shore as well as the sea; and the ice at the North Pole floats on the sea while the South Pole's ice lies on land. None of these makes a sentence false.
